Method of Attack: Distributes Android banking trojan via Google Play Store apps
Uses dropper apps posing as office/productivity apps
Updates clean apps with malicious code after initial submission
Downloads payloads from external GitHub resources
Overlays phishing pages on legitimate banking apps
Performs on-device fraud by automating banking transactions
Converts stolen funds to cryptocurrency and uses money mule networks
Impacted Systems: Nearly 600 financial apps of banking institutions worldwide
Banking apps of customers in the U.S., U.K., Germany, Austria, and Switzerland
Attack Vector: Malicious apps uploaded and updated on Google Play Store
Dropper apps requesting external payloads from GitHub
Phishing overlays and keylogging on infected Android devices
Indicators of Compromise: Malicious dropper apps on Google Play posing as PDF viewers, editors, and office suites
Payloads masqueraded as text recognizer add-ons for Adobe Illustrator downloaded from GitHub
Over 30,000 installations via Google Play in 2023
Previous campaign in November 2021 with over 300,000 installations
